questions.question: What is PyTorch's core training abstraction?
options: A static image of a neural network
Tensor operations recorded for automatic differentiation, followed by an explicit optimizer step
A database transaction that stores every activation forever
A deployment server that chooses the model architecture
questions.explanation: PyTorch executes tensor operations and records differentiable work so backward can compute gradients. The training loop explicitly owns zeroing gradients, backward, and the optimizer update.

questions.question: A run uses micro-batch 2, 8 accumulation steps, and 4 ranks. What is the effective global batch?
questions.explanation: Global batch is micro-batch x accumulation steps x data-parallel ranks: 2 x 8 x 4 = 64.

questions.question: Why can increasing gradient accumulation fail to solve an out-of-memory error?
options: Accumulation always doubles model parameters
It changes optimizer frequency but does not reduce the activation memory of the current micro-batch
It disables automatic differentiation
It forces every rank onto the CPU
questions.explanation: Accumulation increases effective batch across multiple micro-steps. The current micro-batch still determines activation memory, so micro-batch size or checkpointing may need to change.

questions.question: When is FSDP generally considered instead of DDP?
options: When one full copy of model, gradient, and optimizer state does not fit comfortably on each rank
Whenever a model has fewer than ten parameters
Only for CPU inference
When the dataset contains no labels
questions.explanation: DDP replicates model state. FSDP shards state across ranks, trading additional communication and checkpoint complexity for lower per-rank memory.

questions.question: One DDP rank exits while the others are reducing gradients. What is the correct recovery boundary?
options: Continue seven ranks with stale gradients
Restart only the failed Python function
Fail the coordinated process group and resume all ranks from one coherent checkpoint
Delete the distributed sampler
questions.explanation: Synchronous ranks participate in one step and collective membership. The group must restart coherently from shared training and data progress.

questions.question: Which state is required in a robust training checkpoint in addition to model weights?
options: Only the dashboard color theme
Optimizer, scaler, scheduler, progress, RNG, and data position
Only the final validation metric
Every raw training example copied into the file
questions.explanation: A true resume must restore update dynamics and sample progression, not merely load parameters for inference.

questions.question: How should torch.compile be introduced into a production training path?
options: Before establishing an eager correctness and performance baseline
As a measured optimization after correctness, representative shapes, and graph breaks are understood
As a replacement for all tests
Only after removing every dynamic input
questions.explanation: Compilation can improve performance but may graph-break or recompile for changing inputs. Compare it with a correct eager baseline under representative workloads.

questions.question: Which metric most directly exposes a data-loader straggler in synchronous distributed training?
options: Cluster-wide average loss only
Per-rank data-wait, compute, and collective time
The source repository star count
The number of model classes
questions.explanation: Averages hide one slow participant. Per-rank timing separates input starvation from compute and collective pressure.
